issues.legal_issue: A government lease of mineral land does not create a prohibited monopoly or infringe claimants’ rights when they have no established entitlement to the leased area.
material_facts: The government owned the land and its minerals and leased an area to another operator.
The leased area contained no portion previously leased to the petitioners.
The petitioners had excavated limestone in the area before, but showed no legal authority entitling them to have the disputed area leased to them.
issues.conclusion: The lease did not create a monopoly in the limestone business or infringe the petitioners’ fundamental rights.
issues.legal_principle: As owner of land and its minerals, the government was prima facie entitled to lease the area. Without a legal right to that area, the petitioners could not establish that the lease created a monopoly or infringed their rights.

predicates.constitutional_rights_petition: The claimants brought a petition seeking relief for an alleged infringement of constitutional rights.
predicates.government_owns_mineral_land: The government owned the land and the minerals beneath it.
predicates.leased_area_not_previously_held_by_claim: The area leased to another operator was not part of land previously leased to the claimants.
predicates.claimants_show_no_legal_entitlement_to_a: The claimants showed no legal authority giving them a right to have the disputed area leased to them.

issues.definition: When a constitutional-rights petition concerns government-owned mineral land that was not previously held by the claimants, and they show no entitlement to it, the government’s lease creates neither a monopoly nor an infringement of their rights.

issues.legal_issue: A limestone mining lease is not subject to the rules for minor minerals merely because it concerns limestone when the lease does not specify limestone for lime burning and the record does not establish that use.
material_facts: The lease described the subject as limestone but did not state that it was limestone to be used for lime burning.
The record did not establish that the limestone was used only for lime burning.

The applicable rules defined minor minerals to include limestone used for lime burning and excluded minor minerals from their application; the provincial rules for minor minerals had not yet been framed when the lease was granted.
issues.conclusion: The lease was not shown to concern a minor mineral, so the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949 applied and the government’s grant was not illegal on the asserted ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1948 prohibited granting a mining lease otherwise than in accordance with the rules. Under the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949, limestone was a minor mineral when used for lime burning, and Rule 4 excluded minor minerals from those rules. On the lease and record before it, the Court found no basis to treat this lease as one for a minor mineral.

predicates.mining_lease_case: The challenged instrument granted rights to excavate a mineral.
predicates.lease_does_not_specify_limestone_for_lim: The lease described limestone but did not state that it was to be used for lime burning.
predicates.record_does_not_establish_lime_burning_o: The evidence in the record did not establish that the limestone was used only for lime burning.

issues.definition: A mineral lease is not treated as one for a minor mineral where its text does not specify limestone for lime burning and the record does not establish that exclusive use, so it is not invalid on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A petition under Article 32 is unavailable to challenge government action unless the action violates a fundamental right.
material_facts: The petitioners sought relief under Article 32 concerning the government’s grant of a lease to another operator.
The petitioners did not establish a fundamental right to have the disputed area leased to them or otherwise show that the grant infringed a fundamental right.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the government’s action had been illegal, the petition could not be maintained under Article 32 without a violation of a fundamental right.
issues.legal_principle: Article 32 relief requires an infringement of a fundamental right; illegality of government action, without such an infringement, is insufficient to maintain the petition.

predicates.article_32_petition: The claimants sought a constitutional writ through a petition invoking the constitutional remedy for fundamental-rights violations.
predicates.no_fundamental_right_violation_shown: The claimants did not establish that the challenged government action violated a fundamental right.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks relief through a fundamental-rights petition but shows no fundamental-rights violation, that constitutional relief is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to the closure of a mineral-processing operation becomes infructuous when the relevant permission has expired and no right to renewal is established.
material_facts: The petitioners alleged that the government had directed them to close their lime kilns while their permission was still in force.
The permission, even if it amounted to a lease, had ended before the petitions were decided.
The petitioners produced no document establishing a lease, and the document they relied on concerned permission for non-agricultural use of land.
The document required an application for renewal but did not guarantee renewal, and the petitioners showed no right to have the permission renewed.
issues.conclusion: The petitions became infructuous insofar as they challenged the direction to close the kilns; any claim for damages or other relief was not determined by that conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: A challenge to closure based on an expired permission presents no continuing claim to that permission when no right to renewal is established. A requirement to apply for renewal does not itself guarantee renewal.

predicates.constitutional_petition_challenging_clos: The claimants used a constitutional petition to challenge a direction that they stop operating their kilns.
predicates.permission_expired_before_decision: The permission under which the claimants operated had ended before the court decided the petition.
predicates.no_renewal_entitlement_established: The claimants showed no enforceable right to renewal, and the relevant document required an application without guaranteeing renewal.

issues.definition: When a constitutional petition challenges closure under permission that has expired before decision and no renewal entitlement is established, the closure challenge is infructuous.
